program: Infinity, set theory, Cantor — the foundations layer
principle: Cantor's theorem, cardinal/ordinal arithmetic, uncountability. Mathlib-backed. This is the rigorous core of the 'infinity / Cantor' program; phenomenology (Husserl) is treated only where it admits a faithful formal model (e.g. a mereological partial order), never fabricated as a theorem. AXLE gates.

queue.statement: Cantor's theorem: for any type X, no function f : X -> Set X is surjective. (Use Mathlib's Function.cantor_surjective.)
Dual Cantor: for any type X, no function g : Set X -> X is injective. (Use Mathlib's Function.cantor_injective.)
Cantor's cardinal inequality: for every cardinal c, c < 2 ^ c. (Use Mathlib's Cardinal.cantor.)

Cantor-Schroeder-Bernstein: for types X Y, if there is an injection X -> Y and an injection Y -> X then there is a bijection X <-> Y. (Use Mathlib's Function.Embedding.schroederBernstein / Cardinal antisymmetry.)

The real numbers are uncountable: there is no surjection from Nat onto Real; equivalently Real is not a countable type. (Use Mathlib's Cardinal.not_countable_real / Real.not_countable or mk_real = continuum.)
The naturals are countably infinite: Nat is a Countable type and is Infinite. Prove Countable Nat and Infinite Nat.
The rationals are countable: Rat is a Countable type (equivalently Denumerable). (Use Mathlib's instance / Cardinal.mkRat.)
Cardinal arithmetic: aleph_0 + aleph_0 = aleph_0 (Cardinal.aleph0 + Cardinal.aleph0 = Cardinal.aleph0). And aleph_0 * aleph_0 = aleph_0.
Koenig's theorem (a strict-cardinal-sum-vs-product form): if for all i in an index set, a i < b i (cardinals), then Cardinal.sum a < Cardinal.prod b. (Use Mathlib's Cardinal.sum_lt_prod.)

A faithful formal fragment of Husserlian part-whole (mereology): model 'part-of' as a partial order on a type P (reflexive, antisymmetric, transitive) and prove that proper-part-of (strict order) is irreflexive and transitive, and that the whole (a Top element, if present) has every element as a part. Concretely: given [PartialOrder P] [OrderTop P], prove for all x : P, x <= (Top : P), and for all x, not (x < x), and for all x y z, x < y -> y < z -> x < z. (A rigorous formal model of a phenomenological structure, labeled as a MODEL, not a claim about consciousness.)
